name: Equestrian, stables and riding clubs

problems.words: Lessons booked on WhatsApp get double-booked
quick_ideas: Take bookings on one number only
Keep one shared schedule instead of a whiteboard and two phones.

workzap_build.text: lesson booking with instructor and horse assigned, blocking double bookings and sending confirmations right away.

problems.free_stops: The booking rules and confirmation flow go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare this week's lesson chats against the yard diary once, so you see where double-bookings are actually starting.
Give one person the job of writing every lesson booking in one diary, so parents get one clear answer each time.

problems.words: Same horses used too many lessons a day, no record
quick_ideas: Note how many sessions each horse does a day
Agree a limit per horse with your instructor and vet.

workzap_build.text: a horse workload tracker that counts sessions per horse and stops bookings past the stable's own limit.

problems.ask_first: How many horses are used for lessons?
problems.free_stops: How limits are applied to bookings stays in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Mark each horse's lesson turns on paper for one full day, so you can spot which horses carry the busiest load.
Give one groom or instructor the job of updating the horse-use notebook after each lesson, so allocation stops changing mid-day.

problems.words: Instructors cancel last minute and parents get angry
quick_ideas: Keep a note of every cancellation and who made it
Have a standby instructor for busy days.

workzap_build.text: customer_messaging — an instructor schedule with a cancellation log and messages sent to affected parents right when changes happen.

problems.ask_first: How often do cancellations happen in a month?
problems.free_stops: The cancellation process and messaging go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note every same-day instructor cancellation this week and which lesson slot it hit, so the worst pressure points show.
Set one fixed handover time for instructor changes each day, so parents hear about swaps before arriving at the club.

problems.words: Livery owners pay late and we keep feeding their horses
quick_ideas: Send each owner a clear monthly statement
Agree one due date for everyone.

workzap_build.text: livery billing with balances and reminders sent on time.

problems.ask_first: How many horses are on livery?
problems.free_stops: Reminder timing and statement layout are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many horses are still in your stalls with unpaid livery from last month, so today's feeding cost against old bills shows.
Give one staff member the job of marking paid and unpaid livery on the yard board after evening checks, so handovers stop missed follow ups.

problems.words: Extras for livery horses (farrier, vet, transport) never get billed
quick_ideas: Note each extra the day it happens
Add the month's extras to the livery bill.

workzap_build.text: credit_ledger — extras logged as they happen and added straight onto each owner's invoice.

problems.ask_first: Who arranges the farrier and vet visits?
problems.free_stops: How extras are logged and invoiced stays in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare this week's yard extras with what was written for each livery account, so missed charges show before bills go out.
Keep one notebook in the office for all livery extras, so outside costs stop being forgotten at billing time.

problems.words: Package lessons used up but nobody tracks the balance
quick_ideas: Keep a count of lessons used per package
Tell parents when a few lessons are left.

workzap_build.text: loyalty_repeat — package balances that update with every lesson, with renewal reminders sent right on time.

problems.ask_first: Do most riders pay per lesson or in packages?
problems.free_stops: The balance and renewal rules go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many riders have no clear lesson balance written anywhere, so you can see the size of the package-tracking problem.
Give one staff member the package balance list and an end-of-day update time, so used lessons are recorded the same day.

problems.words: Hay and shavings run out unexpectedly
quick_ideas: Count hay and bedding once a week
Note how long a delivery usually lasts.

workzap_build.text: hay, feed and bedding stock with reorder alerts and cost per horse kept updated as you go.

problems.ask_first: Who orders hay and bedding now?
problems.free_stops: Reorder points and the cost view are set out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk the store room and note how many days hay and shavings lasted since the last delivery, so ordering timing gets clearer.
Give one person the stock notebook and one weekly count time, so supplies stop being guessed during busy yard days.

problems.words: Daily care checklists aren't done when I'm away
quick_ideas: Write the daily routine down once, the way you already run it
Ask for a photo when each block is done.

workzap_build.text: a daily care checklist per stable block with timestamps and photos, flagging missed items right away.

problems.ask_first: How many grooms work each day?
problems.free_stops: The checklist and flag rules stay in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Check one week's missed daily checklist items against the days you were away, so you see where the routine breaks.
Give one senior staff member the checklist handover at closing, so unfinished yard jobs are clear before the next shift starts.

problems.words: Summer in Dubai, lessons drop to almost nothing
quick_ideas: Look at early-morning or indoor sessions and school-holiday camps
Get in touch with past riders, with their permission, before the season turns.

workzap_build.text: messages to past riders and parents sent right before camps and the new season.

problems.ask_first: Do you have an indoor or covered arena?
problems.free_stops: Timing and audience for the messages go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare summer lesson attendance with your busiest recent month, so the seasonal drop is clear before staffing decisions.
Give one person a fixed weekly slot to list inactive riders by age group, so quiet weeks get follow-up without last-minute scrambling.

problems.words: Waivers and rider forms are paper and some are missing
quick_ideas: Check which current riders have no form on file
For what the forms should say, talk to your lawyer or insurer.

workzap_build.text: digital rider forms tied to each booking, with missing forms flagged before the lesson.

problems.free_stops: The form flow and booking checks stay in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count rider files missing a signed waiver or form today, so you know how much front-desk chasing is pending.
Give one staff member the rider form folder and end-of-day check, so missing papers stop slipping through busy lesson times.

never_say: Any veterinary, farrier, feeding, medication, training or riding-technique advice, or any view on whether a horse is fit to ride or compete.
Anything that helps with doping, false passports or microchips, illegal import or export, or hiding injuries.
Children's names, schools or photos; riders are recorded by role and age group only.
Legal or insurance advice on waivers; anything to do with gambling on events.

sample_reply.person: We have a riding school in Lahore with 18 horses, mostly kids. Weekend bookings are chaos and some horses end up doing six lessons. What can we do?
sample_reply.pi:
Yes, this can be brought under control, and the first steps are simple.
First, bring all bookings into one shared schedule on one number, so the same slot can't be given twice.
Second, agree a daily limit per horse with your instructor and vet, and keep a count against it.
Workzap's part would be: lesson booking that assigns instructor and horse, blocks double bookings and stops any horse going past its limit.

Shall I put together a solution document and quote for you, or would you rather not?
